title: Transmission 04: record release, no launch
event: Four tracks, cut at 45, five hundred pressed and no more. There is no launch party, no press list, no photograph of anybody and no name on the label beyond a designation and a number. It goes to eleven shops in four cities and to a post office box, and when the five hundred are gone the plates are destroyed.
when: Released 7 September 1992; sleeves and posters ship with the boxes on 1 September
where: Eleven shops: Detroit, Berlin, Rotterdam, London
function: A record release. The poster goes in the shop window and in the sleeve, and it is the only thing anybody will ever see about the record.
stakes: Five hundred copies and no second pressing, so the poster is the entire distribution of meaning. If it reads as a product, the refusal to be a product has failed on its only outing.

hard_constraints.why: The designation is the record's only name. It implies a sequence and refuses a title, which is the position stated in three characters.
A release date on a run of five hundred is a queue instruction. Without it the shops set their own and half the run sits in a stockroom.
The commission fixes the register as well as the facts: nothing on this poster is a sentence. Anything longer than three words is somebody explaining the record.

notes: No artist may be named, including on the reverse. The catalogue number and the box number are the only permitted attributions.
